claims.text: HfZrTiTa0.53 has an as-processed yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has an as-processed compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The reported 13.5% terminal strain for HfZrTiTa0.53 is a tensile elongation.
Controlled post-processing annealing and cooling will produce partial recrystallization in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Controlled post-processing annealing and cooling will create a bimodal grain-size distribution in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The treatment will form dispersed ductile intergranular phases or regions.
Fine grains in the proposed bimodal structure will provide strength.
Coarser ductile intergranular regions will enhance tensile ductility.
The controlled thermal treatment will promote more homogeneous deformation.
Enhanced grain-boundary sliding will be a principal mechanism of the ductility improvement.
The modified microstructure will delay localized necking.
The treatment will increase tensile uniform elongation by at least 50%, from 13.5% to approximately 20% or higher.
The treatment will retain approximately the as-processed compressive strength.
The treatment will retain approximately the as-processed impact-triggered energy release.
The hypothesis applies at room temperature under quasi-static tensile and compression loading at approximately 10^-3 s^-1.
Thin-steel-target penetration is an applicable impact test for treated and untreated HfZrTiTa0.53.
Annealing conditions outside an optimized range may compromise the strength-ductility balance.

contradictions.description: The 13.5% value is called terminal tensile strain or tensile elongation and is then used as the baseline for uniform elongation, although terminal strain and uniform elongation are distinct measurements.
The hypothesis says compressive strength and impact energy release will not be reduced, whereas the falsification rule accepts reductions of up to about 10%.
